source_detail: Built in ca-tools 2026-11-10 in two steps. Step 1, profile product (method of Colbourn and Torres-Jimenez 2013, Thm 4.2 / Cor 4.5; programs/pprod.py) of the table's own CA(15; 2, 20, 3) (CA_15_2_20_3_fd13075b, rows 0 and 3, 5 agreements) and our own CA(20; 2, 61, 3) built on 2026-11-09 (programs/CA_20_2_61_3_ingredient.txt, rows 0 and 3, 13 agreements), giving CA(32; 2, 1155, 3). Step 2, column extension at 32 rows with programs/ext2t.c, one column at a time, each new column the best of 100 or 200 random columns, then simulated annealing with exact pair counts in which only the new column and the merged row of the product may change (temperature 0.7), and a new column that stays stuck for 200000 moves is drawn again; three runs, 1155 to 1242, 1242 to 1322 (command ext2t p32_1155.txt 32 1155 0 87 3 100 0.7 out -chain 80 -frl 1 -ntry 100 -kick 200000 -i previous) and 1322 to 1390. The merged row ended unchanged. Exact check with ca_verify, all column pairs
construction: Profile product of our CA(15; 2, 20, 3) and CA(20; 2, 61, 3), CA(32; 2, 1155, 3), then column extension by simulated annealing to 1390 columns
notes: 32 rows at 1390 columns; the cited 32-row size has 1308 columns; the run was stopped while still gaining; no Torres-Jimenez array is an ingredient or start
